slides: Let's continue with remainders, and write them with a letter.

slides.say: When a number leaves a known remainder, we can write it with a letter. Take numbers that leave three when divided by four. Seven is one four plus three. Eleven is two fours plus three. So each one is some whole fours, plus three. We write it as four k plus three. k tells us how many complete groups of four there are, and k is a whole number.
at: Seven is one four plus three
Eleven is two fours plus three
We write it as four k plus three

slides.say: Why does it work? Four k is always divisible by four, and the three on the end is what's left. k can also be zero. Then the number is just three, and three divided by four leaves three, like five divided by eight before.
at: three divided by four leaves three

slides.say: Another example. A number that leaves four when divided by fifteen is fifteen k plus four. For example, nineteen, thirty-four and forty-nine all leave four when divided by fifteen.

Sometimes a question changes the divisor. A number leaves four when divided by fifteen. What does it leave when divided by five? Write it as fifteen k plus four. Fifteen k is five times three k, a whole number of fives, so it divides by five. So the number divided by five leaves four. Check it with nineteen: nineteen divided by five leaves four.
at: Write it as fifteen k plus four

slides.say: Now a number that leaves thirteen when divided by fifteen. Fifteen k still divides by five, but thirteen is too big to be a remainder by five. So we divide it again. Thirteen is two fives plus three, so the remainder is three. Check it with twenty-eight: twenty-eight divided by five leaves three.
at: Thirteen is two fives plus three

slides.say: But it doesn't always work. A number leaves two when divided by eight. What does it leave when divided by six? Try two, and it leaves two. Try ten, which also leaves two when divided by eight. Ten divided by six leaves four. Two different answers, so we can't know.
at: two when divided by eight. Ten

slides.say: What's the difference? Five divides fifteen, so fifteen k is five times three k. Fifteen k leaves no remainder when divided by five, so only the extra four matters. Six doesn't divide eight. So knowing the remainder by eight doesn't tell us one fixed remainder by six. Our examples gave two and four. So changing the divisor works only when the new divisor divides the old one.
at: fifteen k is five times three k

slides.say: To sum up. For two, five and ten, look at the last digit. For three and nine, the digit sum. For four, the last two digits, and for eight, the last three. A bigger divisor, split it into parts that share no divisor bigger than one.
For eleven, in a three-digit number, the first two digits minus the last one, or the outer digits minus the middle one.

A remainder is what's left in your hand. It's always smaller than the divisor, and the biggest one is the divisor minus one. Now some questions. Come in focused, because remainders are the part that confuses people. [pause] I'll see you in the next video.
